title: Effects of Zinc Oxide Nanoparticle Coating on the Surface Morphology and Streptococcus mutans Adhesion of Stainless Steel Archwires After Intraoral Use: A Split-Mouth Randomized Clinical Study
html: To evaluate Streptococcus mutans adhesion and surface morphology of Zinc Oxide nanoparticle coated stainless steel archwire and to compare it to uncoated stainless steel wires after 4–5 weeks of intraoral use. This randomized clinical trial with a split-mouth design included 18 patients undergoing fixed orthodontic treatment. Each patient received a ZnO nanoparticle coated stainless steel archwire in one arch and an uncoated archwire in the opposing arch. Archwires (0.016″ × 0.022″) were retrieved after 4–5 weeks (mean, 32.1 ± 4 days). Surface roughness was evaluated using atomic force microscopy before and after intraoral exposure. Streptococcus mutans adhesion was assessed using the roll plate method, expressed as colony-forming units (CFU) per wire segment. Surface roughness parameters were compared using paired t-tests; CFU counts, which deviated from normality, were compared using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test, with log-transformed paired t-tests as a sensitivity analysis (α = 0.05). The trial was registered in Clinical Trial Registry- India (CTRI/2025/10/096600). ZnO nanoparticle–coated archwires demonstrated significantly lower roughness values than uncoated wires ( p < 0.001). Mean CFU counts were significantly lower in the coated group (Wilcoxon signed-rank test, p = 0.0008). A significant correlation between surface roughness and bacterial adhesion was observed. ZnO nanoparticle–coated stainless steel archwires showed reduced surface roughness and lower Streptococcus mutans adhesion after intraoral exposure.
